title: Broad Paschen lines as black hole mass tracers: A reverberation mapping calibration
comment: Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A); 12 pages, 9 figures
summary: Single-epoch (SE) black hole mass estimators based on rest-frame ultraviolet or optical broad lines can be limited by dust attenuation or wavelength coverage. We calibrate estimators based on broad Paschen P$α$ and P$β$ directly against reverberation mapping (RM) masses. We obtained LBT/LUCI near-infrared spectra of 27 SDSS-RM quasars and combined them with archival Paschen measurements for AGNs with RM masses. After continuum subtraction, we measured line luminosities and full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) using multi-component and single-Gaussian profile models. We fitted $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=a+b\log(L/10^{41}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}})+c\log({\rm FWHM}/10^3\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}})$, including intrinsic scatter. The fiducial relations use photometrically corrected line luminosities and FWHMs of the combined broad profiles. For P$α$, we obtain $(a,b,c)=(6.86^{+0.24}_{-0.25},0.47^{+0.11}_{-0.10},1.24^{+0.49}_{-0.48})$ with an intrinsic scatter of $0.28^{+0.08}_{-0.06}$ dex. For P$β$, we obtain $(7.00\pm0.24,0.48^{+0.10}_{-0.09},0.91^{+0.46}_{-0.47})$ with a scatter of $0.32^{+0.08}_{-0.06}$ dex. Relations using single-Gaussian widths, 5100 Å continuum luminosities, or fixed virial slopes have scatters consistent within the uncertainties. These relations provide complementary mass estimators when ultraviolet or optical broad lines are attenuated or unavailable. They should be applied within the parameter ranges of the calibration sample and remain subject to the systematic uncertainty associated with the RM virial factor.

AI.tldr: The paper calibrates single-epoch black hole mass estimators using broad Paschen lines (Pα and Pβ) against reverberation mapping masses. Using LBT/LUCI near-infrared spectra of 27 SDSS-RM quasars plus archival data, they derive empirical scaling relations with intrinsic scatter of 0.28 dex (Pα) and 0.32 dex (Pβ), providing alternative mass estimators when UV/optical lines are attenuated or unavailable.
AI.motivation: Single-epoch black hole mass estimators based on UV or optical broad lines suffer from dust attenuation or limited wavelength coverage. Near-infrared Paschen lines (Pα, Pβ) can bypass these issues, but lack calibrated relations against reverberation-mapping masses.
AI.method: Near-infrared spectra of 27 SDSS-RM quasars obtained with LBT/LUCI were combined with archival Paschen measurements for AGNs with RM masses. After continuum subtraction, line luminosities and FWHMs were measured using both multi-component and single-Gaussian profile models. The scaling relations log(M_BH/M_sun) = a + b·log(L/10^41) + c·log(FWHM/10^3) were fitted including intrinsic scatter.
AI.result: For Pα: (a,b,c) = (6.86, 0.47, 1.24) with 0.28 dex scatter. For Pβ: (a,b,c) = (7.00, 0.48, 0.91) with 0.32 dex scatter. Relations using alternative profile measurements or luminosities gave consistent scatter within uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: These calibrated Paschen-line relations provide complementary single-epoch black hole mass estimators when UV/optical broad lines are attenuated or unavailable. They should only be applied within the calibrated parameter ranges and inherit the systematic uncertainty from the RM virial factor.

title: Narrow Population Inference Enhanced by Analytical Likelihood Models
summary: The growing catalog of gravitational-wave events has revealed substantial diversity in the properties of compact-binary mergers. However, commonly used population-inference methods based on discrete posterior samples can struggle to constrain narrow population features, resulting in biased or unstable estimates of population hyperparameters. We first demonstrate this limitation using a toy population model by comparing parameter recovery with a continuous likelihood model against discrete approximations constructed from $10^3$, $10^4$, and $10^5$ samples. We then perform the same comparison using synthetic eccentric and multisource populations introduced in previous studies. Although the continuous and discrete approaches yield broadly consistent results, the continuous approximation more accurately recovers the parameters of narrow simulated populations. In particular, while both methods produce similar mass distributions, appreciable differences arise for narrowly distributed parameters such as spin and eccentricity. Our results indicate that the continuous approach provides more reliable inference for spin and eccentricity, whose narrow population distributions can be inadequately represented by finite sample sets. Continuous likelihood models therefore offer a valuable tool for improving population inference and extracting more robust information about the formation and evolution of compact-binary systems.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that continuous likelihood models for gravitational-wave population inference outperform discrete posterior-sampling methods, particularly for narrow population features such as spin and eccentricity distributions, offering more reliable and robust estimates of population hyperparameters.
AI.motivation: Commonly used population-inference methods based on discrete posterior samples struggle to constrain narrow population features, leading to biased or unstable hyperparameter estimates in the growing catalog of gravitational-wave compact-binary merger events.
AI.method: The authors compare parameter recovery using a continuous likelihood model against discrete approximations constructed from 10^3, 10^4, and 10^5 samples, first on a toy population model and then on synthetic eccentric and multisource populations from previous studies.
AI.result: The continuous approximation more accurately recovers parameters of narrow simulated populations. While both methods produce similar mass distributions, appreciable differences emerge for narrowly distributed parameters such as spin and eccentricity, where finite sample sets inadequately represent the true population.
AI.conclusion: Continuous likelihood models offer a valuable tool for improving population inference and extracting more robust information about the formation and evolution of compact-binary systems, especially for spin and eccentricity parameters with narrow distributions.

title: Spatially resolved molecular gas conditions in the circumnuclear disc of 3C 84
summary: The brightest cluster galaxy NGC 1275, at the centre of the Perseus cluster, hosts the radio-loud AGN 3C 84 and a circumnuclear disc (CND) of cold molecular gas onto which large-scale CO filaments accrete, yet the physical and chemical conditions of the gas in the CND remain poorly constrained. We present a spatially resolved analysis of ALMA CO(2-1), HCN(3-2), and HCO$^+$(3-2) observations at 72 pc. The data are partitioned into beam-sized hexagonal regions and modelled with a Bayesian framework that couples a neural network emulator of time-dependent chemistry (UCLCHEM) with non-LTE radiative transfer (SpectralRadex) to infer the gas density, kinetic temperature, and cosmic ray ionisation rate in each region. All three line ratios peak in the inner disc and decline with radius. The inference shows radial gradients in density ($\log_{10} n({\rm H_2}) \approx 6.3$ to $\sim 5$), kinetic temperature (~200 K to ~160 K), and cosmic ray ionisation rate ($\log_{10}(ζ/ζ_0) \approx 4.9$ to $\sim 3$). Despite the powerful radio AGN, the observed HCN(3-2)/HCO$^+$(3-2) ratio remains $\lesssim 1$ across the disc. Our modelling attributes this to optical depth saturation of HCN(3-2) ($τ\sim 1$-3), which suppresses the intensity ratio even when the HCN abundance exceeds that of HCO$^+$ by a factor of three or more. The HCN/HCO$^+$ intensity ratio therefore cannot be used as an abundance diagnostic without accounting for optical depth, and a low ratio does not necessarily imply weak AGN influence on the chemistry. Azimuthally resolved profiles suggest a localised HCO$^+$/CO enhancement at the western disc boundary, coinciding with the filament-disc accretion interface and consistent with shock processing by velocity shear between the infalling filaments and the rotating disc. These results indicate that the CND is shaped by accretion from its filamentary environment.

AI.tldr: Spatially resolved ALMA observations (72 pc) of CO(2-1), HCN(3-2), and HCO+(3-2) in the circumnuclear disc (CND) of NGC 1275, modelled via a Bayesian framework coupling a neural-network emulator of time-dependent chemistry (UCLCHEM) with non-LTE radiative transfer (SpectralRadex), reveal radial gradients in gas density (log10 n(H2) ~6.3 to ~5), kinetic temperature (~200 to ~160 K), and cosmic ray ionisation rate (log10 ζ/ζ0 ~4.9 to ~3). The HCN/HCO+ intensity ratio remains ≤1 across the disc due to optical depth saturation of HCN(3-2) (τ~1-3), so it cannot serve as an abundance diagnostic. Localised HCO+/CO enhancement at the western disc boundary is attributed to shock processing at the filament-disc accretion interface.
AI.motivation: The physical and chemical conditions of the gas in the circumnuclear disc (CND) of NGC 1275, at the centre of the Perseus cluster, remain poorly constrained despite its importance as the accretion destination for inflowing CO filaments around a powerful radio-loud AGN (3C 84).
AI.method: Resolved ALMA CO(2-1), HCN(3-2), and HCO+(3-2) observations in 72 pc beam-sized hexagonal regions; a Bayesian framework couples a neural-network emulator of time-dependent chemistry (UCLCHEM) with non-LTE radiative transfer (SpectralRadex) to jointly infer gas density, kinetic temperature, and cosmic ray ionisation rate per region.
AI.result: All three line ratios peak in the inner disc and decline radially. Inference reveals radial gradients: density log10 n(H2) from ~6.3 to ~5, kinetic temperature ~200 to ~160 K, and cosmic ray ionisation rate log10(ζ/ζ0) from ~4.9 to ~3. HCN(3-2)/HCO+(3-2) ≤1 across the disc despite HCN abundance up to >3× that of HCO+, explained by optical depth saturation (τ~1-3). Azimuthal profiles show a localised HCO+/CO enhancement at the western disc boundary coincident with the filament-disc accretion interface, attributed to shock processing by velocity shear.
AI.conclusion: The CND is shaped by accretion from its filamentary environment. The HCN/HCO+ intensity ratio is not a reliable abundance tracer without optical depth corrections, and a low ratio does not necessarily imply weak AGN influence on the chemistry.

title: Probing the Three-Dimensional Structure of a Jet with Faraday Tomography
comment: Accepted for publication in Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan (PASJ)
summary:
Magnetic fields play a fundamental role in the dynamics and radiation of jets associated with active galactic nuclei (AGNs), where they accelerate and collimate the relativistic plasma and produce the observed synchrotron emission.
  Faraday tomography is a powerful technique for probing the three-dimensional distribution of magnetic fields and synchrotron-emitting plasma along the line of sight, by reconstructing the Faraday Dispersion Function (FDF) from the observed polarization spectrum.
  To explore what aspects of AGN-jet structure can be revealed by Faraday tomography, we construct a simple three-dimensional model of an AGN jet that captures its essential features, and compute the resulting FDF for a range of model parameters.
  The jet is represented as a cylindrical region of uniform thermal-electron density threaded by a coherent helical magnetic field, to which a random turbulent component can optionally be added.
  The parameters varied include the inclination angle θ between the jet axis and the line of sight, the wavenumber of the helical field, and the amplitude of the random magnetic-field component.
  By systematically varying these parameters, we examine how the underlying magnetic geometry and turbulence are encoded in the observable Faraday and polarization structures. The main observational signatures identified by our model include top-bottom asymmetry across the jet, curved or double peaked FDF profiles and increasingly fragmented Faraday depth structure along longer lines of sight, providing potential diagnostics of large scale helical magnetic fields and small scale turbulent components. These signatures providing a physical framework for interpreting future polarimetric observations of AGN jets from instruments such as LOFAR, MeerKAT, and the VLA.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a simple 3D model of an AGN jet with a coherent helical magnetic field and optional turbulent component to compute Faraday Dispersion Functions via Faraday tomography. By varying inclination angle, helical field wavenumber, and turbulence amplitude, the authors identify observational signatures—top-bottom asymmetry, curved or double-peaked FDF profiles, and fragmented Faraday depth structure—that serve as diagnostics for large-scale helical fields and small-scale turbulence in future polarimetric observations.
AI.motivation: To understand what aspects of AGN-jet magnetic field structure can be revealed by Faraday tomography, since magnetic fields are fundamental to jet acceleration, collimation, and synchrotron radiation.
AI.method: A three-dimensional model of an AGN jet is constructed as a cylindrical region with uniform thermal-electron density threaded by a coherent helical magnetic field, with an optional random turbulent component. The Faraday Dispersion Function is computed for systematically varied parameters including inclination angle, helical field wavenumber, and turbulence amplitude.
AI.result: The model identifies three main observational signatures: (1) top-bottom asymmetry across the jet, (2) curved or double-peaked FDF profiles, and (3) increasingly fragmented Faraday depth structure along longer lines of sight. These encode information about large-scale helical magnetic fields and small-scale turbulent components.
AI.conclusion: The identified signatures provide a physical framework for interpreting future polarimetric observations of AGN jets from instruments such as LOFAR, MeerKAT, and the VLA.

title: The Mass Dependence of the Fundamental Metallicity Relation in Observations and Simulations
comment: 19 pages, 8 figures
summary: The metal content of galaxies provides direct insight into the underlying physical processes that drive galaxy evolution. An example of this is the three-parameter relationship between stellar mass, gas-phase metallicity, and star formation rate, commonly referred to as the Fundamental Metallicity Relation (FMR). Previous studies have suggested that the FMR is redshift-invariant (at $z \lesssim 4$) and fully accounts for the scatter in the mass-metallicity relation (MZR). In this work, we test this 'fundamental' relation in both cosmological simulations (EAGLE, SIMBA, Illustris, IllustrisTNG) and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) observations. We find that the canonical anti-correlation between metallicity and specific star formation rate (sSFR) inverts in massive galaxies ($M_\star \gtrsim 10^{10.5} \mathrm{M}_\odot$) in EAGLE, IllustrisTNG, and SDSS. When including lower star forming galaxies, the positive correlation appears for all four simulations and SDSS. We speculate that this inversion may being driven by strong nuclear outflows (from, e.g., active galactic nuclei or stellar feedback), which quench star formation while simultaneously expelling preferentially enriched gas from the center of the galaxy. We also find that this 'inversion' appears in a number of metallicity diagnostics in observations (though the details depend on diagnostic) and persists out to $z \sim 1$ in the simulations. These results demonstrate that these strong nuclear outflows challenge simple gas regulator-type models and provide a new framework to test models of the baryon cycle in both future simulations and observations.

AI.tldr: This paper tests the Fundamental Metallicity Relation (FMR) in cosmological simulations (EAGLE, SIMBA, Illustris, IllustrisTNG) and SDSS observations, finding that the canonical anti-correlation between metallicity and specific star formation rate inverts in massive galaxies (M* ≳ 10^10.5 M⊙), likely driven by strong nuclear outflows (AGN/stellar feedback) that quench star formation while expelling enriched gas.
AI.motivation: Previous studies proposed that the FMR is redshift-invariant and fully accounts for scatter in the mass-metallicity relation. This work aims to test the 'fundamental' nature of this relation by examining its validity across multiple cosmological simulations and SDSS observations, particularly probing whether the relation holds in massive galaxies where feedback processes may disrupt simple gas-regulator behavior.
AI.method: The authors test the three-parameter relationship (stellar mass, gas-phase metallicity, and star formation rate) in four cosmological simulations—EAGLE, SIMBA, Illustris, and IllustrisTNG—as well as in SDSS observational data. They examine the metallicity-sSFR correlation across stellar mass regimes and redshift, and investigate the possible physical drivers of any deviations from the canonical FMR.
AI.result: The canonical anti-correlation between metallicity and sSFR inverts in massive galaxies (M* ≳ 10^10.5 M⊙) in EAGLE, IllustrisTNG, and SDSS observations. When including lower star-forming galaxies, the positive correlation appears across all four simulations and SDSS. The inversion persists out to z ~ 1 in the simulations and appears across multiple metallicity diagnostics in observations, though the details depend on the diagnostic used.
AI.conclusion: The FMR is not universally valid as a 'fundamental' relation; strong nuclear outflows (e.g., from AGN or stellar feedback) can quench star formation while expelling preferentially enriched gas from galaxy centers, inverting the expected metallicity-sSFR correlation in massive galaxies. This challenges simple gas-regulator models and offers a new framework for testing baryon cycle models in future simulations and observations.

title: Testing the QGP Star Hypothesis: The oMEGACat BH-2 System as a Candidate Color-Superconducting Quark-Gluon Plasma Star
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures
summary: The recent discovery of a long-period binary system in the globular cluster $ω$ Centauri, oMEGACat BH-2 \citep{Whitaker2026}, provides an unprecedented opportunity to probe the true nature of compact dark objects. The system's massive, dark companion has been inferred to have a mass of $4.46_{-1.01}^{+1.22} M_\odot$, which places it in the ``mass gap'' between neutron stars and the canonical stellar-mass black holes. In this Letter, we explore the hypothesis that the oMEGACat BH-2 companion is not a classical black hole, but a stable, self-bound Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP) star, as described by recent general relativistic models that incorporate Nonlinear Electrodynamics (NLED) and the asymptotic freedom of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) \citep{Mosquera2025}. We compare the inferred mass of the companion with the novel Mass-Radius ($M$-$R$) relation predicted by the QGP star model. We find that the inferred mass of the $ω$ Centauri object lies squarely within the wide mass spectrum predicted for hypermassive QGP stars ($0$ to $>7$ $M_\odot$). Although this consistency is not enough for claiming evidence, it suggests that oMEGACat BH-2 may be the first observed candidate for a QGP star, representing a stable, non-singular end-state of stellar collapse. We argue that future astrometric monitoring with JWST and radio-telescopes like FAST and SKA can further constrain the oMEGACat BH-2 orbital parameters. Meanwhile, gravitational-wave follow-ups for the $f$ and $g$ modes by observatories like LIGO, VIRGO, KAGRA, LISA, ET and CE can be crucial for distinguishing a classical black hole from the ``gravitational eternally collapsing `kompact' object'' (\GECKO) state of our QGP star model.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether the massive dark companion in the ω Centauri globular cluster binary system (oMEGACat BH-2, mass ~4.46 M⊙, in the "mass gap") could be a stable self-bound Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP) star rather than a classical black hole, using a general relativistic model with Nonlinear Electrodynamics and QCD asymptotic freedom. The inferred mass falls within the predicted QGP star mass range (0 to >7 M⊙), suggesting it may be the first QGP star candidate, though not conclusive evidence.
AI.motivation: The discovery of oMEGACat BH-2, a compact dark object in the mass gap between neutron stars and canonical stellar-mass black holes, provides an unprecedented opportunity to test whether such objects are truly black holes or alternative compact configurations. The authors seek to explore whether this object could instead be a QGP star, a stable, non-singular end-state of stellar collapse.
AI.method: The authors compare the observationally inferred mass of the oMEGACat BH-2 companion (~4.46 M⊙) with the Mass-Radius (M-R) relation predicted by a general relativistic QGP star model incorporating Nonlinear Electrodynamics (NLED) and QCD asymptotic freedom. They assess consistency with the model's predicted mass spectrum for hypermassive QGP stars, and propose future observational diagnostics including astrometric monitoring (JWST, FAST, SKA) and gravitational-wave mode searches (f and g modes) with advanced detectors (LIGO, VIRGO, KAGRA, LISA, ET, CE).
AI.result: The inferred mass of the ω Centauri object lies squarely within the wide mass spectrum predicted for hypermassive QGP stars (0 to >7 M⊙), making it consistent with a QGP star interpretation. However, this consistency alone is insufficient to claim evidence for a QGP star vs. a classical black hole.
AI.conclusion: oMEGACat BH-2 may be the first observed candidate for a QGP star, representing a stable, non-singular end-state of stellar collapse. Future astrometric and gravitational-wave observations are crucial for distinguishing a classical black hole from the "gravitational eternally collapsing kompact object" (GECKO) state of the QGP star model.

title: Verifying Gamma-Ray Burst Duration Analysis Using the Compton Gamma-Ray Observatory T50 Data
comment: Keywords: gamma-ray burst, gamma-ray, satellites, statistical analysis
summary: Several authors have shown in the literature that a third type of gamma-ray burst class can be detected in the Compton Gamma-Ray Observatory data using T90. In this paper, I examine whether this can also be found in the T50 variable data from the Compton Gamma-Ray Observatory Burst And Transient Source Experiment observation. According to my calculations, the third group detected in T90 can also be detected in the T50 data.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether the third gamma-ray burst (GRB) class previously detected in the T90 duration variable from Compton Gamma-Ray Observatory (CGRO) data can also be identified in the T50 duration variable from the same CGRO BATSE (Burst And Transient Source Experiment) data. The author confirms that the third group is detectable in the T50 data as well.
AI.motivation: Prior studies have shown that a third class of gamma-ray bursts exists beyond the traditionally known two classes (short and long), identifiable in the T90 duration metric. This study aims to determine if this classification holds when using the T50 duration variable instead, testing the robustness of the third-class detection across different duration measures.
AI.method: The author analyzes the T50 duration data from the Compton Gamma-Ray Observatory BATSE observations to check whether a third gamma-ray burst class can be statistically detected, analogous to what was previously found using T90 data. The analysis involves computing and comparing the class structure in the T50 distribution.
AI.result: The calculations show that the third gamma-ray burst class, previously detected using T90, can also be detected in the T50 duration data from CGRO BATSE.
AI.conclusion: The third gamma-ray burst class is a robust feature not limited to the specific T90 duration metric, as it is also recoverable when using the alternative T50 duration variable.

title: Assessing the Credibility of Gamma-Ray QPO Candidates in 41 TeV-Selected Blazars
comment: 21 pages, 9 figures, 7 tables. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)
summary: We analyze quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) candidates in the 0.1-100 GeV Fermi-LAT light curves of 41 TeV blazars with a conservative, multi-stage timing analysis combining FFT power spectra, red-noise Monte Carlo simulations, false-discovery-rate control, bootstrap period uncertainties, split-sample cross-validation, Lomb-Scargle and WWZ diagnostics, a detection-only sensitivity test, observingwindow checks, and injection-recovery experiments. A first-pass FFT search flags 16 sources above a raw 95% level and six strong candidates after data-quality and split-sample filtering, none satisfying a fully automated multi-method tier. Source-level significance is quantified with forward simulations that preserve the observed sampling and non-Gaussian flux distribution, treating the red-noise slope as a nuisance parameter and never assuming independence of periodogram powers. At simulation-selected reference slopes, only two of the 41 sources reach a raw source-level p < 0.05,only J1555.7+1111 reaches Benjamini-Hochberg significance, and none survives Benjamini-Yekutieli correction. No source survives the conservative slope envelope. Even J1555.7+1111, which the first-pass search flagged as significant but did not rank among its strong candidates, has a global p-value that rises to 7.5*10^-3 under the least favorable slope (~ 0.31 after the full-sample search), so it is not a robust detection. With substantial period uncertainties, a weak observing window, and limited injection-recovery sensitivity, we establish no robust gamma-ray QPO detection: a sampling-faithful red-noise treatment substantially contracts the candidate set, providing an explicit assessment of QPO credibility.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a conservative, multi-stage timing analysis of 0.1-100 GeV Fermi-LAT light curves from 41 TeV blazars searching for quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs). Despite initial flagging of several candidates, only one source (J1555.7+1111) reaches Benjamini-Hochberg significance under favorable assumptions, and none survive conservative corrections or slope-envelope checks. The authors conclude there is no robust gamma-ray QPO detection.
AI.motivation: To rigorously assess the credibility of QPO candidates in TeV blazar gamma-ray light curves, addressing the prevalence of false positives in prior QPO claims by applying a maximally conservative, sampling-faithful statistical framework.
AI.method: Multi-stage timing analysis combining FFT power spectra, red-noise Monte Carlo simulations, false-discovery-rate control, bootstrap period uncertainties, split-sample cross-validation, Lomb-Scargle and WWZ diagnostics, sensitivity tests, observing-window checks, and injection-recovery experiments. Forward simulations preserve observed sampling and non-Gaussian flux distributions, treating red-noise slope as a nuisance parameter without assuming independence of periodogram powers.
AI.result: First-pass FFT flagged 16 sources above raw 95% level and 6 strong candidates after filtering, but none fully survived the automated multi-method tier. Only 2 of 41 sources reached raw source-level p < 0.05 at simulation-selected slopes; only J1555.7+1111 reached Benjamini-Hochberg significance; none survived Benjamini-Yekutieli correction or the conservative slope envelope. The best candidate's global p-value rose to ~0.31 under full-sample search.
AI.conclusion: No robust gamma-ray QPO detection is established among the 41 TeV blazars. A sampling-faithful red-noise treatment substantially contracts the candidate set, providing an explicit assessment of QPO credibility and cautioning against optimistic QPO claims in Fermi-LAT data.

title: A Broadband X-ray Analysis and Optical Counterpart Search of IC5052 ULX
comment: 17 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We present broadband X-ray spectral and timing analysis of the Ultra-luminous X-ray source (ULX) in IC5052 using simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations from 2022, supplemented by archival 2013 XMM-Newton data. A two-thermal component model, often interpreted as radially-segregated emission from a super-Eddington inner disc and its associated wind, provides a statistically acceptable fit but yields an implausibly high inner disc temperature of $k T_\mathrm{in} \approx 6.4$ keV, inconsistent with even super-Eddington disc models. Including an additional continuum component from either an accretion column or a Comptonizing corona, as motivated by high S/N observations from other ULXs, provides comparable goodness of fit while allowing plausible inner disc temperatures. The accretion column model yields $k T_\mathrm{in} \approx 1.2$ keV with the column contributing $F_\mathrm{col} \approx 62\%$ of total flux, while the Comptonizing corona model yields $k T_\mathrm{in} \approx 3.0$ keV with a scattered fraction $\sim 1$, assuming the hotter disc provides the seed photons. Timing analysis initially challenges both scenarios: the accretion column model places IC5052 ULX where prior results suggest pulsations may be detectable ($F_\mathrm{col} \sim 62\%$), yet none were detected, while the corona model appears inconsistent with its lack of observed short-timescale variability. However, incorporating spectral information relaxes these constraints, allowing both models to remain physically plausible for IC5052 ULX. Finally, using improved Chandra astrometry, we identified a candidate optical counterpart consistent with an evolved high mass donor. A discrepancy between the optical extinction and X-ray fitted absorption suggests localised X-ray absorption.

AI.tldr: The authors analyze broadband X-ray observations of the ULX in IC5052 using simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR data from 2022 plus archival 2013 data. They test two-thermal and three-component spectral models, finding that an additional continuum component (accretion column or Comptonizing corona) allows physically plausible inner disc temperatures. Timing analysis challenges both scenarios but incorporating spectral information keeps both models viable. They also identify a candidate optical counterpart with an evolved high-mass donor and find evidence for localized X-ray absorption.
AI.motivation: To determine the physical nature of the ULX in IC5052 by distinguishing between competing spectral models (two-thermal vs. accretion column vs. Comptonizing corona) and assessing their consistency with timing and multiwavelength observations.
AI.method: Broadband X-ray spectral and timing analysis of simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations (2022), supplemented by archival 2013 XMM-Newton data. Spectral fitting with multiple physical models, timing variability analysis, and improved Chandra astrometry for optical counterpart identification.
AI.result: The two-thermal model fits well but gives an implausible inner disc temperature (~6.4 keV). Adding an accretion column (kT_in ~1.2 keV, contributing ~62% of flux) or a Comptonizing corona (kT_in ~3.0 keV) yields plausible temperatures. Timing initially disfavors both scenarios (no pulsations found for the column model; no short-timescale variability for the corona model), but spectral information relaxes these constraints. A candidate optical counterpart consistent with an evolved high-mass donor was identified, with a discrepancy suggesting localized X-ray absorption.
AI.conclusion: Both the accretion column and Comptonizing corona scenarios remain physically plausible for IC5052 ULX when spectral information is incorporated. The source likely harbors a super-Eddington accretion flow, and the optical/X-ray absorption discrepancy indicates localized X-ray absorption along the line of sight.

title: Arcminute Microkelvin Imager observations at 15.5 GHz of the tidal disruption event Swift J164449.3+573451 from 2011 Mar to 2014 Mar

The results from 308 observations made from 2011 Mar to 2014 Mar are presented. These show a steady rise in flux density from $\approx$3 mJy (three days after the initial $γ$-ray detection of Swift J164449.3+573451), to a peak of nearly 30 mJy $\approx$140 days later, followed by a steady decline.

AI.method: Radio monitoring at 15.5 GHz using the Arcminute Microkelvin Imager (AMI), with 308 observations spanning from March 2011 to March 2014.

title: Quantum-Gravity-Inspired Effects in Neutron Stars: A Critical Map from Microscopic Assumptions to Observables
comment: 33 pages, 4 figures. Review article
summary: Claims that neutron stars constrain quantum gravity often compare models whose new physics enters at different stages of the stellar calculation. This article provides a critical map of three representative routes: generalized-uncertainty-principle deformations of microscopic thermodynamics, noncommutative-inspired modifications of the effective matter source, and higher-curvature or scale-dependent modifications of gravitational dynamics. For each route we identify the quantity that is changed, the dimensionless parameter controlling the correction, and the consistency conditions required before masses, radii, or tidal deformabilities can be compared with observations. A deformed phase-space measure must be implemented in a thermodynamically consistent interacting equation of state; a smeared density must be completed by a conserved stress-energy tensor, generally with anisotropic pressure; and a gravitational effective field theory must remain within its derivative expansion and be applied consistently to both the equilibrium background and tidal perturbations. Simple scale estimates show that coefficients of natural size suppressed by the Planck scale are negligible in neutron stars. Observable effects consequently constrain model-dependent effective scales or enhanced couplings, not microscopic quantum gravity directly. The resulting framework is intended to separate robust phenomenological bounds from effects produced by inconsistent implementations or by degeneracies with the high-density equation of state.

AI.tldr: This paper critically maps three representative routes through which quantum gravity could affect neutron stars (GUP-deformed thermodynamics, noncommutative-inspired matter modifications, and higher-curvature/scale-dependent gravitational dynamics), identifying for each the altered quantity, controlling dimensionless parameter, and consistency conditions. The authors show that Planck-scale-suppressed corrections are negligible in neutron stars, so observable effects only constrain model-dependent effective scales or enhanced couplings—not microscopic quantum gravity directly.
AI.motivation: Claims that neutron stars constrain quantum gravity often compare models whose new physics enters at different stages of the stellar calculation, making comparisons misleading. A systematic framework is needed to separate robust phenomenological bounds from artifacts of inconsistent implementations or degeneracies with the high-density equation of state.
AI.method: The authors analyze three representative routes to quantum-gravity effects in neutron stars: (1) generalized-uncertainty-principle (GUP) deformations of microscopic thermodynamics, (2) noncommutative-inspired modifications of the effective matter source (smeared energy density), and (3) higher-curvature or scale-dependent modifications of gravitational dynamics. For each route they identify the changed quantity, the dimensionless control parameter, and the consistency conditions (e.g., thermodynamically consistent EoS, conserved stress-energy tensor with anisotropic pressure, validity of derivative expansion for both background and tidal perturbations). They then perform simple scale estimates for Planck-scale-suppressed coefficients.
AI.result: Simple scale estimates show that coefficients of natural size suppressed by the Planck scale are negligible in neutron-star observables. Any observable effects must therefore arise from model-dependent effective scales or enhanced couplings. Observable neutron-star data constrain these enhanced/model-dependent parameters, not microscopic quantum gravity directly.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a critical map for separating robust phenomenological constraints from spurious effects due to inconsistent implementations of quantum-gravity-inspired models, and from degeneracies with the unknown high-density equation of state. This helps clarify what neutron-star observations can and cannot actually say about quantum gravity.

title: Supernova 1987A was a "failed supernova" twenty thousand years before its jet-driven explosion
comment: It will be submitted in two days to allow for comments (including missing references)
summary: I show that the progenitor of supernova (SN) 1987A faded substantially and became red for hundreds of years to observers in and near the plane of the equatorial ring, because the equatorial ring, which was formed by a binary interaction between the SN 1987A progenitor and a main-sequence companion that ejected material about 20,000 years before the explosion, obscured the progenitor. For a few hundred years, the luminosity for such hypothetical observers was mainly light scattered by the two outer rings, which amounted to ~5% of the progenitor luminosity. In present terms, this event would have been classified as a "failed supernova" by these observers, although there was no core collapse, no black hole formation, and nothing failed. Rather, this event was a type II ILOT (intermediate-luminosity optical transient), in which equatorial ejecta temporarily obscured the central source. After a few hundred years, the outer rings became transparent, the inner ring became more transparent, and the SN 1987A progenitor brightened over a few thousand years to its normal luminosity for equatorial observers. This finding strengthens the claim that "failed supernova" candidates are likely to be type II ILOTs. Although the binary interaction also spun up the core, the bipolar morphology of SN 1987A (its Keyhole) is misaligned with the triple-ring system. I use the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) to speculate on a scenario that might explain this misalignment. This study adds small but unique support to the claim that the JJEM is the primary explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

AI.tldr: The progenitor of SN 1987A faded and reddened for hundreds of years for observers near the equatorial ring plane because the equatorial ring, formed by a binary interaction ejecting material ~20,000 years before explosion, obscured the star. This temporary obscuration would have been misclassified as a "failed supernova" and is identified as a type II ILOT. After a few hundred years, the ring became transparent and the star returned to normal luminosity. The study also uses the JJEM to speculate on the misalignment between the bipolar Keyhole morphology and the triple-ring system, supporting JJEM as the primary CCSN explosion mechanism.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that the SN 1987A progenitor appeared to fade substantially and become red for hundreds of years to equatorial observers due to obscuration by the equatorial ring, which would have been misinterpreted as a "failed supernova," thereby strengthening the claim that failed supernova candidates are actually type II ILOTs, and to explore the misalignment between the bipolar morphology and triple-ring system using the JJEM.
AI.method: The study analyzes the geometry and light-scattering properties of the triple-ring system around SN 1987A, showing that the equatorial ring obscured the progenitor for observers in/near the ring plane. It models the luminosity as scattered light from the two outer rings (~5% of progenitor luminosity) during the obscuration period, then examines the transparency recovery of the rings over time. The study also applies the JJEM to speculate on the misalignment between the bipolar Keyhole morphology and the triple-ring system.
AI.result: The progenitor faded and reddened for hundreds of years for equatorial-plane observers, with luminosity dominated by outer ring scattering at ~5% of normal. This would have been classified as a "failed supernova" though no core collapse occurred. After a few hundred years the rings became transparent and the progenitor brightened back to normal over a few thousand years. The JJEM provides a plausible scenario for the misalignment between the bipolar morphology and the triple-ring system.
AI.conclusion: "Failed supernova" candidates are likely type II ILOTs where equatorial ejecta temporarily obscure the central source. The study provides small but unique support for the JJEM as the primary explosion mechanism of core-collapse supernovae.

title: Measurement of spin-orbit misalignment in binary black holes via the total spin
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures
summary: The degree of spin-orbit alignment in merging binary black holes is a powerful probe of their formation history. However, assessing spin-orbit misalignment in individual events remains challenging, as most parameters commonly used to characterize precession tend to be poorly constrained. In this work, we introduce the angle between the total spin and orbital angular momentum, $θ_{LS}$, as an alternative measure of spin-orbit misalignment. Using synthetic observations, we show that $θ_{LS}$ retains more information to discriminate between the aligned- and isotropic-spins hypotheses than commonly used alternatives, including $χ_{\rm p}$. We then study this parameter on binary black hole mergers observed in the GWTC-5.0 catalog, and identify multiple events that are inconsistent with having aligned spins. In several of the examples, this is not apparent from the posteriors of the effective spin parameters ($χ_{\rm p}$ or $χ_\mathrm{eff}$) nor the individual spin-orbit tilts ($θ_1$ or $θ_2$) alone, and thus had not been previously identified. We highlight GW241127_061008 as a compelling case for a second-generation merger, with a large, tilted primary spin, unequal masses, and a large primary mass near the pair-instability-supernova mass gap. Finally, we perform population inference using $\cosθ_{LS}$ and confirm that the binary black hole population is inconsistent with either a purely isotropic or a purely aligned-spin distribution, and requires substantial spin-orbit misalignment.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces θ_LS, the angle between total spin and orbital angular momentum, as a more effective measure of spin-orbit misalignment in merging binary black holes. Using synthetic observations, it shows θ_LS retains more discriminative power between aligned- and isotropic-spin hypotheses than commonly used parameters like χ_p. Applying this to GWTC-5.0 events, the authors identify multiple misaligned mergers previously missed, including GW241127_061008 as a candidate second-generation merger. Population inference with cosθ_LS confirms the binary black hole population requires substantial spin-orbit misalignment and is inconsistent with purely aligned or isotropic spin distributions.
AI.motivation: Spin-orbit alignment in merging binary black holes is a key probe of their formation history, but standard parameters used to characterize precession (e.g., χ_p) are often poorly constrained for individual events, making it difficult to identify misaligned systems.
AI.method: The authors propose θ_LS (angle between total spin and orbital angular momentum) as an alternative misalignment measure. title: Thermal Stability of Radiation-Pressure-Dominated Accretion Disks Threaded by Net Vertical Magnetic Flux
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The classical radiation-pressure instability predicts strong thermal variability in luminous black-hole accretion disks, whereas most disk-dominated X-ray binary soft states remain comparatively stable. We examine whether net vertical magnetic flux can weaken this instability through its contribution to the radial stress. The stability depends not only on the equilibrium magnetic stress but also on how that stress changes during a thermal perturbation. We write the local stability condition in terms of the logarithmic heating response, $q_+<q_{+,\rm crit}$, which avoids specifying how the turbulent stress is divided into reference and net-flux components. For the illustrative closure $δ=ζ\sqrt{\bpol\btor}/α$, $\etad=-d\lnδ/d\ln H$ describes the response of the fractional stress correction, while $\Gnf=d\ln W_{\rm nf}/d\ln H$ describes the response of the additional net-flux stress itself. For an accretion disk around a $10M_\odot$ black hole at $R=20\rg$ and $\Mdot=0.5\MEdd$, we adopt fixed local mass flux on the thermal timescale, $(γ,\gp)=(1,0)$, and $d\lnζ/d\ln H=0$. Marginal stability then occurs at $\bpol^{\rm crit}=0.0176$ for $ζ=1$ and $0.1338$ for $ζ=0.25$. These thresholds depend on the adopted stress closure and field-response prescription and should not be interpreted as universal magnetic-pressure fractions. title: The GPSP Atlas: High-resolution Galactic Photon Survival Probability Atlas for Very-High- and Ultra-High-Energy Gamma-Ray Astronomy
comment: 29 pages, 15 figures. Published in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ). Public release of the GPSP and GPSP-LIV atlases, including FITS data products and Python helper modules. Data available via Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/21403524. Documentation and example notebooks available at https://gpsp-atlas.readthedocs.io
summary: The emergence of Galactic PeV astronomy makes photon--photon ($γγ$) absorption an increasingly important component of gamma-ray data analysis. In this work, the Galactic Photon Survival Probability (GPSP) atlas is presented as the first Galactic framework describing gamma-ray survival probabilities over the full parameter space $P(l,b,d,E_γ)$ between 1 TeV and 10 PeV. The atlas is constructed using two independent GALPROP-based interstellar radiation field (ISRF) models, allowing direct assessment of ISRF-related systematics, and is released in a FITS format compatible with standard analysis frameworks. A novel gamma-ray survival phase space representation is introduced, extending 1D survival profiles into a 2D energy--distance framework that visualizes Galactic transparency and gamma-ray horizons. Using the full atlas, Galactic transparency and Galactic plane survival maps are constructed. These reveal that Galactic opacity is highly structured, with enhanced attenuation along spiral-arm tangent directions in the $\sim$100--300 TeV regime, while attenuation becomes nearly isotropic and cosmic microwave background (CMB) dominated near PeV energies. The framework naturally accommodates attenuation calculations for extended and diffuse sources. The atlas is further extended to subluminal Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) scenarios through the GPSP-LIV atlas, incorporating LIV-modified pair production kinematics and cross sections. Sources emitting in the 2--3 PeV regime beyond gamma-ray horizons are identified as promising targets for probing LIV effects. Finally, practical applications are presented for the Galactic Center PeVatron and the Cygnus X-3 regions. The GPSP and GPSP-LIV atlases establish a publicly available foundation for studies of Galactic PeVatrons, diffuse gamma-ray emission, and fundamental physics searches in the emerging era of Galactic PeV astronomy.

title: Across the Universe: GW231123 as a magnified and diffracted black hole merger
comment: 20 pages, 12 figures. Accepted in ApJL. Posterior samples: https://zenodo.org/records/20217942 ; code: https://github.com/miguelzuma/GW231123_lensing_PLS
summary: GW231123 appears as the most massive binary black hole (BBH) ever observed by the LIGO interferometers with total mass $190-265 M_\odot$. A high observed mass can be explained by the combination of cosmological redshift and gravitational magnification if the source is aligned with a gravitational lens, such as a galaxy. Small-scale objects such as stars and remnants diffract the signal, distorting the wavefront and providing additional lensing signatures. Here we present an analysis of GW231123 combining for the first time the effects of diffraction by a small-scale lens and gravitational magnification by an external potential, modelled as an embedded point-mass lens (PL), finding an intriguing case for the lensing hypothesis. Lensing is favoured by the data, with a false alarm probability of the observed Bayes factors bounded below $<1\%$, or $\sim 2.6 σ$ confidence level. Including lensing lowers the total source mass of GW231123 to $100-180 M_\odot$, closer to BBHs reported so far, and also removes discrepancies between different waveform approximants and the need for high component spins. We reconstruct all source and lens properties, including the microlens mass $190-850 M_\odot$, its offset, the magnitude of the external gravitational potential and its orientation. The embedded PL analysis leads to a lighter microlens compared to the isolated PL. Within our assumptions, the reconstruction is complete up to an ambiguity between the distance and projected density (mass-sheet degeneracy). Assuming a single galaxy as the macroscopic lens allows us to infer the total amplification of the signal, placing the event at redshift $0.7-2$, and predict the probability $~55\%$ of forming an additional detectable image due to strong lensing by the macrolens. We discuss the implications of our findings on the source and nature of the microlens, including a possible dark matter origin.
